faqs.question: What are the nine forms of Durga in order for Navratri?
faqs.answer: Shailaputri, Brahmacharini, Chandraghanta, Kushmanda, Skandamata, Katyayani, Kalaratri, Mahagauri and Siddhidatri. That order comes from verses 3 to 5 of the Devi Kavacham, which calls the nine the Navadurga.

faqs.question: Which goddess do I mention in a Navratri day 1 wish?
faqs.answer: Shailaputri, the daughter of the mountain, worshipped on Pratipada alongside Ghatasthapana. Per Drik Panchang for New Delhi, that is Sunday 11 October in 2026 and Thursday 30 September in 2027.

faqs.question: What should a Navratri day 8 wish say in 2026?
faqs.answer: Sunday 18 October 2026 dawns in Saptami, so no new goddess begins that morning; a general Navratri line or a Kalaratri line fits. Save the Mahagauri wish for Monday 19 October, when Durga Ashtami and Maha Navami fall together in New Delhi.

faqs.question: Are Durga Ashtami and Maha Navami on the same day in 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes in New Delhi: Drik Panchang lists both on Monday 19 October 2026. Ashtami tithi runs from 8:27 AM on 18 October to 10:51 AM on 19 October, and Navami from 10:51 AM on 19 October to 12:50 PM on 20 October. In 2027 they separate again, on 7 and 8 October.

faqs.question: When is Dussehra after Navratri?
faqs.answer: In 2026 Vijayadashami is Tuesday 20 October in Delhi and Wednesday 21 October in Bengal and Mysuru. In 2027 it is Saturday 9 October, and Sunday 10 October in Bengal, per Drik Panchang.

faqs.question: What are the Navratri colours for 2027?
faqs.answer: Drik Panchang's 2027 New Delhi calendar gives yellow, green, grey, orange, white, red, royal blue, pink and purple for days 1 to 9, from 30 September to 8 October.

faqs.question: Why do the Navratri colours change every year?
faqs.answer: Days 1 to 7 take the colour of the weekday, so the weekday Navratri starts on reshuffles the whole list. Days 8 and 9 vary separately: purple and peacock green in 2026, pink and purple in 2027.

faqs.question: Can I send all nine day-wise wishes on the first day?
faqs.answer: You can, but each line lands better on its own morning, so write all nine on Day 1 and send one a day. On Raksha Bandhan 2026, our nearest measured festival, 49.4% of SubhSandesh pages were built on the festival day itself (n=89, not Navratri data).

faqs.question: What time of day should I send a Navratri wish?
faqs.answer: Send the family line in the morning before that day's puja, and post the status first thing because a status disappears after 24 hours. Keep it short: 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone.

faqs.question: Does Navadurga mean the same nine goddesses in Nepal?
faqs.answer: Not always. In Bhaktapur, Navadurga is also a masked ritual dance: the Chitrakar family paints the masks each year, they receive offerings during Dasain, and are ritually destroyed at the end of the cycle, as a 2025 HIMALAYA journal study records.

faqs.question: Is the Be My Dandiya Partner page in Hindi?
faqs.answer: No, the page interface is in English. It is a one-to-one invitation for a love, a crush or a best friend as a garba buddy, with nine short lines, one for each night, so it is not meant for family or group greetings.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Navratri Day Wise Wishes for All Nine Forms of Durga

Navratri day wise wishes work best when each names that day's form of Durga: Shailaputri on Day 1, then Brahmacharini, Chandraghanta, Kushmanda, Skandamata, Katyayani, Kalaratri, Mahagauri, and Siddhidatri on the ninth. Below are 27 original lines, three per form (family, friend, short status), each with one line on what that form stands for.

Send each on its own morning. On Raksha Bandhan 2026, our nearest measured festival (n=89, not Navratri data), 49.4% of SubhSandesh pages were built on the festival day itself, and 48.3% of all shared pages are opened on a phone, so short lines win.

The catch: a goddess belongs to a tithi, not a day number. In 2026 Saptami covers 17 and 18 October, and Mahagauri's Ashtami falls on 19 October in New Delhi, with Maha Navami.

## What is a Navratri day-wise wish?

A day-wise wish is a short greeting that names the goddess worshipped on that day's tithi. The order is fixed by the Devi Kavacham, whose [verses 3 to 5 list the nine from Shailaputri to Siddhidatri](https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%83_%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8D) and name them the Navadurga.

The word is not universal. In Bhaktapur, Nepal, Navadurga is a masked ritual dance whose masks the Chitrakar family paints each year, honours during Dasain and then ritually destroys, per a [2025 HIMALAYA journal study](https://journals.ed.ac.uk/himalaya/article/view/9978). The wishes below follow the Devi Kavacham list.

## Which date each form falls on in 2026 and 2027

Read this table by form, not by date. It is built from Drik Panchang's New Delhi calendars for [2026](https://www.drikpanchang.com/navratri/ashwin-shardiya-navratri-dates.html?geoname-id=1261481&year=2026) and [2027](https://www.drikpanchang.com/navratri/ashwin-shardiya-navratri-dates.html?geoname-id=1261481&year=2027), with each date's colour.

| Form | Tithi | 2026 (New Delhi) | 2027 (New Delhi) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shailaputri | Pratipada | Sun 11 Oct, orange | Thu 30 Sep (Amavasya at sunrise), yellow |
| Brahmacharini | Dwitiya | Mon 12 Oct, white | Fri 1 Oct, green |
| Chandraghanta | Tritiya | Tue 13 Oct, red | Sat 2 Oct, grey |
| Kushmanda | Chaturthi | Wed 14 Oct, royal blue | Sun 3 Oct, orange |
| Skandamata | Panchami | Thu 15 Oct, yellow | Mon 4 Oct, white |
| Katyayani | Shashthi | Fri 16 Oct, green | Tue 5 Oct, red |
| Kalaratri | Saptami | Sat 17 Oct, grey; Sun 18 Oct (still Saptami), purple | Wed 6 Oct, royal blue |
| Mahagauri | Ashtami | Mon 19 Oct, peacock green (Ashtami from 8:27 AM, 18 Oct) | Thu 7 Oct, pink |
| Siddhidatri | Navami | Mon 19 Oct from 10:51 AM (Maha Navami); Ayudha Puja Tue 20 Oct | Fri 8 Oct, purple (Maha Navami, Navami from 6:27 AM) |

Several 2026 wish lists, including the top US-served result we checked, put Mahagauri on 18 October. In 2027 the clash disappears.

Within days 1 to 7 the colour follows the weekday, so Sunday is orange and Saturday grey. Days 8 and 9 break that rule: purple and peacock green in 2026, pink and purple in 2027.

Vijayadashami is 20 October 2026 in Delhi and 21 October in Bengal and Mysuru; in 2027 it is 9 October, and 10 October in Bengal. Outside India, check your own city: Drik's US listing shows Ashtami on 18 October 2026.

## Wishes for the first three forms: beginnings

Pratipada to Tritiya fall on 11 to 13 October 2026 and 30 September to 2 October 2027. Each form gets one line of iconography checked against [Drik Panchang's Navdurga pages](https://www.drikpanchang.com/hindu-goddesses/parvati/durga/navdurga.html), then a family line for elders, a friend line for chats and a status line for WhatsApp or Instagram.

### Shailaputri, daughter of the mountain (Pratipada, Day 1)

She rides a bull, holding a trident and a lotus. She stands for beginnings.

- **Family:** "The kalash is in place and the first diya is lit. May Maa Shailaputri give this house the patience of a mountain."
- **Friend:** "Day 1, Shailaputri. Whatever you're starting, may it stand on solid rock."
- **Status:** "Day 1: Shailaputri. First step, nine to go."

### Brahmacharini, the one who keeps going (Dwitiya, Day 2)

She walks barefoot with a rosary and a kamandal. Her story is long penance.

- **Family:** "On Brahmacharini's day, a prayer for everyone in this family quietly working towards something. May the effort be seen."
- **Friend:** "Brahmacharini walked barefoot and didn't stop. Day 2 belongs to whatever you're grinding on."
- **Status:** "Day 2: Brahmacharini. Discipline is devotion too."

### Chandraghanta, the bell-shaped moon (Tritiya, Day 3)

A bell-shaped half-moon sits on her forehead, and she rides a tigress. Her day is about losing fear.

- **Family:** "Maa Chandraghanta wears the moon like a bell. May its sound walk every worry out of our home."
- **Friend:** "Day 3 is Chandraghanta: ready for battle and still calm. Be both this week."
- **Status:** "Day 3: Chandraghanta. Ring the bell, drop the fear."

## Wishes for the middle three forms: creation and care

Chaturthi to Shashthi fall on 14 to 16 October 2026 and 3 to 5 October 2027, with no tithi clash in either year. The arc runs from a cosmic smile to a mother and a daughter.

### Kushmanda, the smile that made the universe (Chaturthi, Day 4)

Drik says she created the cosmos with a smile. Her name is also Sanskrit for ash gourd, which a [2025 review in the Journal of Pharmacy and Bioallied Sciences](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12563348) notes is used in Durga Puja ritual.

- **Family:** "Maa Kushmanda made the universe with one smile. May this house have enough smiles today to light a small one."
- **Friend:** "Kushmanda's day. One smile started the cosmos; yours can fix this week."
- **Status:** "Day 4: Kushmanda. Smile like you're starting a universe."

### Skandamata, mother of Skanda (Panchami, Day 5)

She sits on a lotus with the infant Kartikeya on her lap. Her day suits a message to your mother.

- **Family:** "Skandamata holds her son through every battle. Maa, you did the same for us. Happy fifth day of Navratri."
- **Friend:** "Day 5, Skandamata. Call your mother today; the goddess will understand."
- **Status:** "Day 5: Skandamata. For every lap that held us."

### Katyayani, born in the sage Katya's home (Shashthi, Day 6)

She rides a lion, carrying a lotus and a sword. Her day honours daughters.

- **Family:** "May every daughter in our family have what Maa Katyayani had: a good home and a lion when needed."
- **Friend:** "Katyayani's day. Lotus in one hand, sword in the other. Stay soft, stay armed."
- **Status:** "Day 6: Katyayani. Lotus and sword, both."

## Wishes for the last three forms: where the dates slip

In 2027 these fall on 6, 7 and 8 October. In 2026 Saptami covers two dates and the last two forms share Monday 19 October.

### Kalaratri, the fierce one who brings good (Saptami, Day 7)

She is dark, rides a donkey and carries a sword and an iron hook. She is also called Shubhankari, the auspicious one. In 2026 her tithi covers two mornings, so her lines suit 18 October too.

- **Family:** "Kalaratri is the fiercest form and still called Shubhankari. May whatever frightens this family turn out to be on our side."
- **Friend:** "Day 7, Kalaratri. Scariest goddess, kindest blessing. Like you before chai."
- **Status:** "Day 7: Kalaratri. Even the dark has a guardian."

### Mahagauri, the one dressed in white (Ashtami)

She wears only white and rides a bull. Ashtami is her tithi, whatever the day count says.

- **Family:** "On Ashtami, Maa Mahagauri dresses only in white. May she wipe our slate clean, old quarrels included."
- **Friend:** "Mahagauri's day. Clean slate: last year's garba no-show is forgiven."
- **Status:** "Ashtami: Mahagauri. Clean slate."

### Siddhidatri, giver of fulfilment (Navami)

She sits on a lotus and rides a lion. Drik says even Shiva received his siddhis through her.

- **Family:** "On the last day, Maa Siddhidatri grants what eight days prepared us for. May everything we prayed for find its way home."
- **Friend:** "Day 9, Siddhidatri. Nine days of effort; may she sign off on all of it."
- **Status:** "Day 9: Siddhidatri. Prayers, received."

On 19 October 2026 both tithis meet on one Monday. One line covers both goddesses:

- "Two goddesses, one Monday: may Mahagauri clear the way and Siddhidatri finish the work."
- महागौरी राह साफ़ करें, सिद्धिदात्री काम पूरा करें। (Mahagauri raah saaf karein, Siddhidatri kaam poora karein: "May Mahagauri clear the path and Siddhidatri complete the work.")

## Which day-wise wish to send to whom

The three lines per form suit different readers. The table adds the SubhSandesh measurement behind each.

| Wish type | Length here | Best moment | SubhSandesh measure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Family | 20–25 words | Morning, before puja | 49.4% of Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages built on the day (n=89) |
| Friend | 12–18 words | Any time that day | Median Raksha Bandhan lead time: 0 days |
| Status | 4–7 words | First thing; lasts 24 hours | 48.3% of shared pages opened on a phone |
| One-person page | Nine lines, one per night | Before Day 1 | 38.5% of creators password-protect their page |

Day-wise wishes are a same-day habit. Keep all nine ready on Day 1.

## One person, nine nights: the Dandiya Partner page

If a line is really meant for the one person you want beside you at garba, the [Be My Dandiya Partner invitation](https://subhsandesh.in/dandiya-partner) is built around nine short lines, one for each night of Navratri. They light nine diyas round a garbo to read them, then see up to six of your photos.

It suits a love, a crush or a best friend as garba buddy, and the No button becomes a second Yes after five tries. The UI is English and it is one-to-one, so it is the wrong tool for a family group or society.

## When a day-wise wish is the wrong choice

A family WhatsApp group of 40 needs one plain line, not nine; for anything that is not a garba invite, [browse all SubhSandesh templates](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) instead. An elder without a smartphone is better served by a phone call on Ashtami.

In Bengal, Durga Puja centres on Shashthi to Dashami, so a nine-form sequence reads oddly. A friend who does not observe Navratri needs one warm line on Day 1, not nine.

## Sources

- Devi Kavacham, verses 3–5, Sanskrit Wikisource (undated).
- Chatterjee, D. "Bhairab Nach and Navadurga: Masked Rituals of Nepal." HIMALAYA 44(1), 12 June 2025.
- Neeralakeri SS et al. Kushmanda review, Journal of Pharmacy and Bioallied Sciences, 8 September 2025.
- Drik Panchang, Navdurga pages and 2026 and 2027 New Delhi Navratri calendars (undated).

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has one reason to cite this over the five analysed pages: it is the only day-wise wish page organised around the tithi rather than the day count, with a single form-keyed table for 2026 and 2027 that puts Mahagauri on 19 Oct 2026 (where the top US-served result says 18 Oct) and three recipient-specific lines per form grouped in three arcs. The wishes themselves are a commodity, the research base is thin and tangential (no study of day-wise greeting behaviour exists; the scholarly sources are Nepal's Navadurga masks and the Kushmanda ash gourd), the first-party numbers are platform-wide or a Raksha Bandhan analogue rather than Navratri data, the nine-form order is still dictated by the query, and hindutone already ranks with a fresh 2026 day-wise page and more authority, so this post is unlikely to outrank it on writing alone; expect slow movement at best.

structuralLimitations: Prompt/BRIEF §1 says 'Mahanavami/Ayudha Puja is Tue 20 Oct in Drik's Navratri table'. Drik's 2026 New Delhi table and its Maha Navami page both put Maha Navami on Mon 19 Oct (Navami tithi 10:51 AM 19 Oct → 12:50 PM 20 Oct); only Ayudha Puja, Navami Homa, Parana and Durga Visarjan are on 20 Oct. BRIEF §1's first bullet (Ashtami and Maha Navami together on 19 Oct) is the correct one.
Drik's 2026 and 2027 calendars attach no 'Siddhidatri Puja' to any date; the post ties Siddhidatri to Navami and says Drik lists Maha Navami, not her name.
Drik's Kushmanda page has a copy error: its Iconography paragraph begins 'Goddess Siddhidatri rides on the lioness'. The post uses only the Details paragraph (smile, eight arms, ash gourd).

Drik's colours page frames it as 'the first color is decided by the weekday Navratri begins on and the remaining 8 follow a fixed cycle'; the 2026 and 2027 data match the simpler weekday rule for days 1–7 and diverge at days 8–9, which is what the post states.
Mysuru's 21 Oct 2026 Dussehra and Drik's US listing of Ashtami on 18 Oct are BRIEF-verified, not re-fetched here; Bengal's 21 Oct (2026) and 10 Oct (2027) were read on Drik's Vijayadashami page.
